title: Polynomial-Time Bound for a Key-Recovery Search
summary: No polynomial-time bound is proved for the attack’s message-space search; determine whether such a bound holds for an attack with constant key-recovery probability.

formal_statement.body: In the proposed key-recovery attack, the procedure $\phi_{V,i}$ searches the message space for a message $M$ satisfying $\operatorname{Hip}(V,E(K,i,\varepsilon,M))=K[i]$, with $i$ used as the nonce and $\varepsilon$ as the header. Its output enables an adversary to compute $\operatorname{Hip}(V,C)$ and recover $K[i]$, repeating for $i=1,\ldots,k$ to recover $K$. Determine whether the search by $\phi_{V,i}$ has a polynomial-time bound, in particular for an attack having constant key-recovery probability; without such a bound, the strategy is not proved to be a polynomial-time attack.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key cryptanalysis of a message-search-based key-recovery attack.
parameters: V: value used by the search procedure and the Hip computation
i: index of the recovered key component and nonce for that search, ranging from 1 to k
M: message sought in the message space
epsilon: header supplied to the encryption call
C: ciphertext used to compute the recovered key component
k: number of indexed recovery iterations used to recover K
key-recovery probability: required to be constant in the highlighted attack case
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the message-space search is polynomially bounded, particularly for an attack with constant key-recovery probability.

citations.label: Authenticated and Misuse-Resistant Encryption of Key-Dependent Data

progress.summary: The source explains how a successful message search yields each indexed key component, then identifies the absence of a runtime analysis as the gap preventing a polynomial-time attack claim. It highlights constant key-recovery probability as the relevant success regime.
citation_labels: Mihir Bellare et al., Authenticated and Misuse-Resistant Encryption of Key-Dependent Data
